comments.note: TagEditorViewModel.cs: SaveAsync calls UpdateTagAsync/CreateTagAsync then individually calls RemoveGrantAsync/AddGrantAsync per changed edge. These operations are not wrapped in a transaction — a failure partway through leaves the tag updated but grants partially reconciled. A higher-level transaction or a repository method for batch grant reconciliation would be safer.

TagEditorViewModel.cs: _originalGrantedTagIds is captured at construction time. If the user's tag-editing session spans a DataChanged event from another mutation (unlikely but possible), the original grant snapshot may be stale. Refreshing on dialog open would be safer.

TagEditorViewModel.cs: SaveAsync does not reset IsBusy = false on success before firing CloseRequested (it only resets it in the catch block). If CloseRequested doesn't close the dialog (edge case), IsBusy stays true. Consider setting IsBusy = false before the fire-and-forget event.

TagEditorView.axaml: ComboBox for SelectedParentTag shows AvailableTags but has no explicit 'None' option to clear to root-level once a parent is selected. The PlaceholderText appears only when nothing is selected. Users have no UI way to change an existing tag back to root-level unless ComboBox supports clearing to null via keyboard. Recommend adding a '— None —' sentinel item.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified and met.
AC1: SaveAsync clamps weight via Math.Clamp(Weight, TagConstants.MinWeight=-10, TagConstants.MaxWeight=10) before building the Tag record and before CloseRequested fires.

AC2: OnSelectedParentTagChanged calls WouldCreateParentCycle; sets _hasCycleError=true and ParentError message; calls SaveCommand.NotifyCanExecuteChanged(). CanSave() checks !_hasCycleError. Verified in source.
AC3: AddGrant() calls WouldCreateGrantCycle when TagId != 0; sets GrantError message and returns without appending to Grants collection. Duplicate guard also present.

AC4: DeleteCommand (CanDelete: IsExistingTag && DeleteImpact==null) fetches GetDeleteImpactAsync and sets DeleteImpact. ConfirmDeleteCommand (CanConfirmDelete: DeleteImpact!=null) only enabled after impact is shown.
AC5: Full solution build confirmed 0 errors, 0 warnings. Regression: 288 App.Tests passed, 0 failed.

comments.note: No unit tests exist for TagEditorViewModel. FakeTagsManager is available in TestHelpers but unused here. A future WP should add tests covering: (a) SaveAsync clamps Weight=15 to 10 and Weight=-15 to -10; (b) CanSave returns false when _hasCycleError=true; (c) AddGrant with cycle returns early and sets GrantError; (d) DeleteAsync sets DeleteImpact; (e) ConfirmDeleteAsync fires CloseRequested(null).

TagEditorViewModel.SaveAsync: IsBusy is reset to false only in the catch block, not on the success path. If CloseRequested fires but the dialog remains open (edge case), IsBusy stays true indefinitely, preventing further saves. Developer already noted this. Consider setting IsBusy=false before invoking CloseRequested.

TagEditorView.axaml (from developer note): ComboBox for SelectedParentTag has no explicit '\u2014 None \u2014' sentinel item. Users cannot clear an existing parent back to null via the UI combo box. This prevents changing a child tag to a root tag. Recommend adding a null-sentinel option before ship.

summary: PASS — WP-011 delivers a well-structured Tag Editor ViewModel and dialog service.
ITagEditorService interface is clean: ShowAsync(Tag?) returns Task<Tag?> with honest CancellationToken-not-observed documentation.
TagEditorViewModel: correct use of CommunityToolkit.Mvvm partial properties and RelayCommand CanExecute guards. CanSave = !_hasCycleError && !IsNullOrWhiteSpace(Name) is correct.
Cycle detection: parent cycle check skipped for new tags (TagId==0); grant cycle check also skipped for new tags — both are correct since new tags are not in the graph yet.
Weight clamping applied before building the Tag record. Grant reconciliation via Except() is elegant and correct.
AvaloniaTagEditorService: event handler subscribed then unsubscribed in finally — no memory leak.
Applied Fix-Forward: IsBusy=false added to success path before CloseRequested fires (was only in catch path).
Known open item: parent ComboBox lacks null-sentinel to clear back to root-level — must be addressed before M7 ships.

comments.note: TagEditorViewModel.SaveAsync: IsBusy was only reset in the catch block, not on the success path. Applied Fix-Forward: moved IsBusy=false to immediately before CloseRequested fires on the success path. This ensures IsBusy is false if the dialog stays open after the event (e.g., the close handler throws or is not wired). Non-behavioral for the normal close path. Build verified: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

AvaloniaTagEditorService: Correctly unsubscribes viewModel.CloseRequested in a finally block after ShowDialog. This is the correct pattern for modal dialog lifetime management — no memory leak risk here.
